workspace-bound-agent-grant-01.graded_text: Each agent connection is bound to one firm workspace chosen at consent and approved by that firm's Admin, and a consultant who works for several firms makes a separate connection for each.

votes.e: C/project/docs/agent-access.md:7 "Every agent connection is bound to exactly one firm workspace for its whole life. A consultant who works for three firms makes three connections. Each one is approved by that firm's Admin"; :76 "The binding can't be changed"; :87 Admin approves at /w/<workspaceId>/settings/agent-connections. Firm is chosen in the authorization flow (step 3, :84-86): at the provider's consent where supported, otherwise on a Harbor Ledger page right after consent, before any data flows or approval.

workspace-bound-agent-grant-02.graded_text: The server checks on every call that the target belongs to the connection's bound workspace and that the consultant's membership and role are still live, so removal from a firm cuts off an existing connection.

votes.e: C/project/docs/agent-access.md:100 "Live membership. The subject must currently be a member of the bound firm... If the membership is gone, the connection moves to `ended` and the call is refused."; :99 "The target workspace is always `connection.workspaceId`"; :102 "Every workpaper id and every list query is resolved inside the bound workspace only"; :44 effective capability uses "the consultant's current role"; :116 test "Removing the consultant from firm A ends the A connection".

workspace-bound-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The design offers no connection whose scope spans more than one firm.

votes.e: Checked C/project/docs/agent-access.md, C/answer.txt, C/diff.txt (only adds the doc). :11 rejects account-wide grant: "An account-wide grant would let one connection reach every firm... that is what the contracts forbid." The closest thing to cross-firm is :127 "The consultant's cross-firm `/agent-connections` page shows only their own connection metadata, never any workpaper content". That is a signed-in UI page, not an agent connection. Enterprise-managed auth (:140) also keeps "The firm-binding and Admin-approval rules".

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] The membership-check source contradicts its own guarantee. C/project/docs/agent-access.md:100 says "Read their current role from verified provider data or our webhook-synced mirror", while :131 says "The gate also catches this on the next call even if the webhook is late, because step 4 rechecks membership live." If the engineer picks the mirror, a late webhook leaves a removed consultant's connection working, and the doc doesn't say which source is required. (withdrawn)

[opus-for-opus2] The fallback chain is circular for the provider the doc names. Assumption 2 (C/project/docs/agent-access.md:147) says that without `providerGrantId` "the fallback is to require organization-scoped tokens selected at consent (flow step 3, preferred path)", but Assumption 3 (:148) says "Clerk's consent doesn't select an organization". If both turn out true, the doc gives no buildable way to tell two firm connections apart, and the gap is deferred ("the gap gets recorded here"). (held)
